Status.note:
This placeholder comes from the 2023 resource plan of Public Service Company of New Mexico. The newer 2026 plan no longer carries it.

2023 plan:
- Open https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf and go to PDF page 218, which is printed page 210. Table 69, Most-Cost Effective Portfolio, shows the Natural Gas row rising to 832 MW in 2037, from 700 MW the year before. That is the 132 MW in 2037.
- The same table shows Natural Gas at zero in 2040 and a Hydrogen CT row of 586 MW in 2040. These are the timepoint 2 conversion units.

2026 plan:
- Open https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf and go to PDF page 177, printed page 162, in the table of modeling assumptions. The New Resources Pending Approval row says 'A new 172 MW combustion turbine is included as a proxy unit in 2029 in all portfolios.' That is the only new gas unit in the plan before 2036.
- PDF page 229, Table 9-1 continued, lists Combustion Turbines Gas/H2 as 0 MW through 2036 and 179 MW at most through 2045. No 2037, 2038 or 2039 gas unit of this size appears.
- PDF page 177 also says 'Operating life of Reeves (146 MW) is extended through 2044' and that other existing gas units stay in service through 2044. So the 2040 retirement date no longer holds either.

Why cancelled and not renamed:
- The 2026 plan filed on September 1, 2026 replaces the 2023 plan. Its new gas placeholder is 172 MW in 2029, not this size or year. The queue row IA-PNM-2025-20 at the Reeves substation matches that 172 MW unit, not this one.
- This is one document, so the status change is medium confidence.

The plan treats new combustion turbines as firm grid peaking capacity and models them as grid resources, with no backup role. Table 69 on PDF page 218 counts them under Firm Generating Resources. No page says backup power in those words, so this is implied and medium.

qa.question: Should this 2023 plan placeholder be cancelled now that the 2026 plan drops it?
qa.finding: The 2023 plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf adds 132 MW in 2037 on PDF page 218, Table 69. The 2026 plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf has no gas unit of that size or year and adds only a 172 MW proxy unit in 2029 on PDF page 177.
qa.recommendation: Accept the cancelled status and the cancellation year of 2026 for both units of this plant. If you accept it, also remove the start year and the planned retirement year by hand, since a cancelled unit carries neither.
qa.note: Open https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2026-irp_final_report_only_sc-pdf, PDF page 177, row New Resources Pending Approval, and PDF page 229, the table of resource additions. The queue row IA-PNM-2025-20 for 172 MW of gas at the Reeves substation in 2029 is in the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory queue file at https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/LBNL_Ix_Queue_Data_File_thru2025.xlsx. It matches the 172 MW proxy unit, so it should be handled as one new unit with the Reeves plant, not by renaming this record.

qa.finding: The name 1, timepoint 1 IRP does not follow the timepoint form of a name, a comma, a space and the word timepoint with a number. The extra word IRP is the only part that breaks the form.
qa.recommendation: Rename it to 1, timepoint 1 so it follows the form. If the unit is cancelled, the name can still be fixed the same way.

qa.question: Should the timepoint 1 unit keep a blank conversion field?
qa.finding: The 2023 plan at https://www.pnm.com/documents/d/pnm.com/pnm-2023-irp-final-pdf, PDF page 151, says new turbines run on natural gas and are assumed to convert to hydrogen in 2040. Timepoint 1 is the gas phase, so it replaces and converts nothing.
qa.recommendation: Leave the conversion fields blank on the timepoint 1 unit, because no earlier unit is named. The conversion is recorded on the timepoint 2 unit, which already points back to G100001092790.
qa.note: Open the plan and read the paragraph above Table 45 on PDF page 151, printed page 143.

GEM's point is 32.91086, -105.92500, which is only a stand-in.
qa.recommendation: Leave the point, the approximate accuracy and the blank City as they are.
